card.name: Just before the word equivalent
card.fires_on: The last piece of a drug or substance name (prednisone, morphine, CO2) right where the word "equivalent" is expected next. Also words in dose-conversion instructions such as "convert ... to a".

modes.label: Drug name before equivalent
modes.description: The end of a drug name in a dose limit, where "or equivalent" or "equivalents" follows.
modes.example: reduce corticosteroid dose to 10 mg or less of prednis<<one>> or equivalent per day within 12

modes.description: Small words in instructions to convert one opioid dose to a total daily dose of another.

modes.label: Gas emissions
modes.description: The 2 in CO2 before "equivalent" in climate text.
modes.example: annual emissions of greenhouse gases would be cut by around 7 (Gt) of CO<<2>> equivalent by 2020.

card.writes: It makes the word "equivalent" (and its forms) more likely to come next.
card.plain: It fires when a dose or amount is about to be given as an "equivalent" of another drug or substance.
